correctness.rationale: The lower-Wythoff indicator is exactly floor((m+1)/phi)-floor(m/phi), hence is the rotation condition {m/phi}>=phi^-2; complementarity gives the upper indicator. The representation count is therefore an interval count for the golden rotation. Direct interval geometry gives the three pieces of Lambda. A convergent-block proof gives uniform O(log N) interval discrepancy because the continued fraction has bounded partial quotients and every N has a Fibonacci/Ostrowski block decomposition of logarithmic length. Equidistribution gives the weak law, and bounded-variation discrepancy plus Abel summation gives the summatory term. The embedded finite replay checks normalization only and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recent paper resolves only the exceptional multiplicities 0, 1, and 2 for a natural Wythoff representation function. The theorem describes the entire representation count on its natural linear scale, explains its oscillations through a one-dimensional rotation phase, and gives an explicit limiting measure with an atom plus a summatory constant. This is a structural global complement, not a routine finite extension or table computation.
